gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Quilon tapers gently wherever its strokes bend and turn, which gives headlines an editorial edge. And Noto Sans Osmanya keeps the paragraphs moving, its s shapes turning wide and easy, its lowercase large beside the capitals.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Thick strokes that lead the eye without bullying it. Quilon brings that editorial confidence, and Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong lets it breathe beside low-contrast rounds that gap like a cracked bangle under a high-set x-height.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Quilon moves through moderate shading, round and straight strokes carrying slightly different weights, which gives its display lines an editorial, commanding presence. Noto Sans Palmyrene keeps text moving, its curves stopping short of closing.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-hau: Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau brings open-ended curves and capitals only a short step above its lowercase, giving the text a modern feel. Quilon above it thickens and thins in gentle steps.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans PhagsPa, with see-through openings and a gentle bump up to capitals. Quilon is the commanding editorial voice, bending its strokes with a mild taper.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Editorial and commanding: Quilon holds the top with gently modulated strokes. But Noto Sans Phoenician does the quiet work, with s curves opening wide at both ends and generous lowercase height.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahla: Quilon: commanding, editorial, horizontals a notch lighter than its uprights. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi then settles into text with gaping e mouths and barely rising capitals, so a full page moves along approachably.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Sharp and editorial, Quilon keeps thin strokes at a respectable weight. Noto Sans Rejang then reads with wide, porthole-like counters, so lines of text feel open and unhurried from start to finish.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-runic: Quilon lets its stroke weight vary moderately, giving headings an editorial, commanding voice. Noto Sans Runic stays out of the way beneath, with a large x-height, tight ascender room, and curves that never fold back on themselves.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Approachable Noto Sans Samaritan lets daylight into its curves, beneath a Quilon heading whose arch shoulders thin slowly into lighter joins. Make Quilon small and that slow thinning goes unnoticed.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-saurashtra: Quiet authority: Quilon shades its strokes lightly, with no harsh thin spots anywhere. And Noto Sans Saurashtra adds counters that stay open to the outside, which is where this pairing really wins.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-sc: Quilon brings medium-contrast strokes and a commanding, editorial tone to the top. Noto Sans SC follows with chalky curves that stop short of closing, so text moves along lightly.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-sharada: A mild thick-thin variation, like a letterpress slug, gives Quilon its editorial authority at display sizes. Noto Sans Sharada simply does the plain work of bulky, open-formed lowercase.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Quilon has hairline-free thin strokes beside weighty stems. It carries the commanding headline voice, while Noto Sans Siddham handles the text with a large central band and an s whose ends hang wide open.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Curves with the slight thickening of a reed pen give Quilon its editorial edge. Noto Sans Sinhala lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase, so a page of text feels dense and steady.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo reads big and open, with a sizable x-height, plus curved letters whose mouths stay wide. Quilon supplies the drama through stroke contrast; the body simply carries the words.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Quilon arrives with commanding, editorial presence, its curves carrying only modest stress. Noto Sans Sundanese backs it with open-mouthed e crossbars and capitals barely taller than the lowercase.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Clean, editorial and quietly commanding, Quilon eases the reading pace with mild shifts in stroke weight across its curves. Noto Sans Sunuwar then lets daylight through every curve beneath it.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri keeps its ascenders short and its x-height generous, with an a whose lower bowl opens up. Quilon handles the drama; this one handles the paragraphs.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-syriac-easter: Commanding from the first glance, Quilon lets mild but visible contrast carry its editorial headings. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern, meanwhile, does the gentler job, with lowercase rising above small caps and curve endings that keep their distance.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-syriac-wester: Quilon shifts weight modestly within each stroke, which gives its display lines an editorial, commanding grip. Yet Noto Sans Syriac Western supports it beneath, holding its terminals far from the stroke body, small letters packed like bundled cable.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Quilon opens with commanding, editorial presence, its stroke modulation tempered and its big a, e and s wide open. Noto Sans Tagalog is the quiet one, its middle zone dominating each line.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Open curves, clear gaps and lowercase filling most of the height make long text go down smoothly. Noto Sans Tagbanwa delivers that beneath Quilon, whose thin strokes are only slightly lighter than its thick ones.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Quilon keeps a restful line, its stroke weight swinging only modestly, with an editorial, commanding air. And Noto Sans Tai Le joins it with ink strokes that taper out before touching and a minimal step from cap to lowercase.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Noto Sans Tai Viet is a sans-serif with short ascenders, a lofty x-height, and terminals pulled back from where curves close. But if Quilon is made small, its restrained weight gaps fade from view.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-takri: Noto Sans Takri reads high-waisted and contemporary, with every small round letter left generously unclosed at the curve. Quilon, with its modest dip in the thin strokes, adds the commanding edge.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Big, bold, almost magnified: Noto Sans Tamil looks enlarged at any size, with terminals stopping far from the stem. Quilon thins out modestly where its curves turn; leave the body size generous.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tamil-supplem: Contemporary and clean, Noto Sans Tamil Supplement draws round forms like open parentheses inside a middle band so tall the line looks stocky. Quilon, with tempered modulation, feels more editorial beside it.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Quilon's strokes swell and thin by just enough to feel editorial, never fussy. And Noto Sans Tangsa follows with wide, welcoming round letters and stubby ascenders that keep paragraphs easygoing.
gen-fs-bevellier-fs-bespoke-sans: Bevellier looks stencil-cut, its single-weight strokes crowded tight together and its lowercase standing high and wide. Bespoke Sans is sharper and more spacious, with curves that stop well short of the stem.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear opens each letter like a pried oyster shell, lofty in its x-height. Preahvihear stays breezy across a full page of text, a sans that sits comfortably under the bent-tubing letterforms of Nippo.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-pt-sans-caption: Drafting-pen steady and cut like wire, Nippo looks technical at a glance. PT Sans Caption brings inviting, unclosed bowls and big-bodied lowercase, and that warmth set against the drafted precision of Nippo is the best thing here.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-puritan: Puritan has a friendly, rounded read, with oversized counters in the e and a that stay clearly open to the side. Nippo, hairline-free and shadow-free, supplies the crisp edge: softness meets precision.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-questrial: Questrial reads open and modern, its round letters wide-mouthed and its strokes uniform in weight, with short stalks above the lowercase. And Nippo supplies the edge, its wire-cut letters nearly capital-sized even in lowercase.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-radio-canada: Wiry and technical up top: Nippo's lowercase stands almost at capital size, each stroke looking cut from wire. Radio Canada answers with full, upright c, s and z.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-radio-canada-big: Technical and contemporary, Nippo looks cut from wire, its small letters nearly capital-sized. Radio Canada Big takes over below as a plain sans, monoline, with terminals finishing clear of the stem and an x-height filling the line.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro reads steadily, with broad gaps at the terminals and an unvarying weight from word to word. Nippo adds a technical edge up top, with proud small letters and wire-cut strokes.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-ruda: Approachable and clean, Ruda has wide-mouthed rounds and a sizable x-height in its lowercase. Nippo and Ruda both look drawn with wire, and that shared thread is what holds the pair.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-saira: Technical in spirit, Nippo draws its nearly capital-sized lowercase with one constant pen width, like wire. Saira follows with rounded letters reaching toward the top line and an s you can see through, which is the pair's real strength.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch is approachable and easygoing, its lowercase e opening clearly and its ascenders sitting close above the x-height. Nippo above it has no calligraphic shading to guide the eye.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-gidole: Gidole keeps every stroke the same as if drawn in neon tube, with terminals held apart like open scissor blades. But Quilon's soft swelling and thinning never goes flat or stark, and that gentle give is what makes the pair.
